arxiv-1906-08771.title: Submodular Batch Selection for Training Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-1906-08771.creator: K J Joseph, Vamshi Teja R, Krishnakant Singh, Vineeth N Balasubramanian
arxiv-1906-08771.description: Abstract Mini-batch gradient descent based methods are the de facto algorithms for training neural network architectures today. We introduce a mini-batch selection strategy based on submodular function maximization. Our novel submodular formulation captures the informativeness of each sample and diversity of the whole subset.

arxiv-2210-12605.title: Keep CALM and CRDT On
arxiv-2210-12605.creator: Shadaj Laddad, Conor Power, Mae Milano, Alvin Cheung, Natacha Crooks, Joseph M. Hellerstein
arxiv-2210-12605.description: Abstract . Despite decades of research and practical experience, developers have few tools for programming reliable distributed applications without resorting to expensive coordination techniques. Conflict-free replicated datatypes (CRDTs) are a promising line of work that enable coordination-free replication and offer certain eventual consistency guarantees in a relatively simple object-oriented API.

arxiv-2211-08805.title: Interacting Hand-Object Pose Estimation via Dense Mutual Attention
arxiv-2211-08805.creator: Rong Wang, Wei Mao, Hongdong Li
arxiv-2211-08805.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rong Wang, Wei Mao, Hongdong Li. 3D hand-object pose estimation is the key to the success of many computer vision applications. The main focus of this task is to effectively model the interaction between the hand and an object. To this end, existing works either rely on interaction constraints in a computationally-expensive iterative optimization, or consider only a sparse correlation between sampled hand and object keypoints.

arxiv-2212-11156.title: Injectivity, stability, and positive definiteness of max filtering
arxiv-2212-11156.creator: Dustin G. Mixon, Yousef Qaddura
arxiv-2212-11156.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dustin G. Mixon, Yousef Qaddura. Given a real inner product space V V and a group G G of linear isometries, max filtering offers a rich class of G G -invariant maps. In this paper, we identify nearly sharp conditions under which these maps injectively embed the orbit space V / G V/G into Euclidean space, and when G G is finite, we estimate the map’s distortion of the quotient metric. We also characterize when max filtering is a positive definite kernel.

arxiv-2308-09247.title: Point Contrastive Prediction with Semantic Clustering for Self-Supervised Learning on Point Cloud Videos
arxiv-2308-09247.creator: Xiaoxiao Sheng, Zhiqiang Shen, Gang Xiao, Longguang Wang, Yulan Guo, Hehe Fan
arxiv-2308-09247.description: Abstract We propose a unified point cloud video self-supervised learning framework for object-centric and scene-centric data. Previous methods commonly conduct representation learning at the clip or frame level and cannot well capture fine-grained semantics. Instead of contrasting the representations of clips or frames, in this paper, we propose a unified self-supervised framework by conducting contrastive learning at the point level.

arxiv-2409-17080.title: Can Vision Language Models Learn from Visual Demonstrations of Ambiguous Spatial Reasoning?
arxiv-2409-17080.creator: Bowen Zhao, Leo Parker Dirac, Paulina Varshavskaya
arxiv-2409-17080.description: Abstract Large vision-language models (VLMs) have become state-of-the-art for many computer vision tasks, with in-context learning (ICL) as a popular adaptation strategy for new ones. But can VLMs learn novel concepts purely from visual demonstrations, or are they limited to adapting to the output format of ICL examples?

arxiv-2602-09842.title: Step-Size Stability in Stochastic Optimization: A Theoretical Perspective
arxiv-2602-09842.creator: Fabian Schaipp, Robert M. Gower, Adrien Taylor
arxiv-2602-09842.description: Abstract We present a theoretical analysis of stochastic optimization methods in terms of their sensitivity with respect to the step size. We identify a key quantity that, for each method, describes how the performance degrades as the step size becomes too large. For convex problems, we show that this quantity directly impacts the suboptimality bound of the method.

pmc-10625482.title: Selective recording of physiologically evoked neural activity in a mixed autonomic nerve using a minimally invasive array
pmc-10625482.creator: Sophie C Payne, Peregrine B Osborne, Alex Thompson, Calvin D Eiber, Janet R Keast, James B Fallon
pmc-10625482.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Real-time closed-loop control of neuromodulation devices requires long-term monitoring of neural activity in the peripheral nervous system. Although many signal extraction methods exist, few are both clinically viable and designed for extracting small signals from fragile peripheral visceral nerves. Here, we report that our minimally invasive recording and analysis technology extracts low to negative signal to noise ratio (SNR) neural activity from a visceral nerve with a high degree of specificity for fiber type and class.

pmc-11428723.creator: Yuefei Feng, Yao Zheng, Dong Huang, Jie Wei, Tianci Liu, Yinyan Wang, Yang Liu
pmc-11428723.description: The registration of preoperative and follow-up brain MRI, which is crucial in illustrating patients’ responses to treatments and providing guidance for postoperative therapy, presents significant challenges. These challenges stem from the considerable deformation of brain tissue and the areas of non-correspondence due to surgical intervention and postoperative changes.

pmc-12514427.title: Enhanced Functional and Surgical Outcomes With 3D Printing in Orthopedic Oncology: A Comparative Meta‐Analysis Against Conventional Techniques
pmc-12514427.creator: Peter Joseph Mounsef, Benjamin Blackman, Ojasvi Sharma, Ahmed Aoude, Anthony Bozzo
pmc-12514427.description: IntroductionThree‐dimensional printing (3DP) technology has increasingly gained attention in orthopedic oncology, where complex tumor resections and reconstructions demand high precision. 3DP enables the creation of patient‐specific models and prostheses, which can improve postoperative quality of life for patients while assisting surgeons in preoperative planning, enhancing surgical accuracy, and improving outcomes in complex oncologic cases.

pmc-12641745.title: Preparation of Suaeda Tea Through Semi-Solid Fermentation Utilizing Kluyveromyces marxianus, Komagataeibacter europaeus, and Acetobacter schutzenbachii: Physicochemical Characteristics, Process Optimization, and Antioxidant Activity
pmc-12641745.creator: Aoqi Dong, Xiaoying Dong, Xinying Dai, Yanru Gao, Yuewen Ning, Xiya Fan, Haiyan Liu
pmc-12641745.description: Suaeda salsa, an annual herb belonging to the genus Suaeda within the Chenopodiaceae family, is highly salt-tolerant and can thrive in large quantities on saline and alkaline soils. This study presents a novel fermentation technique to produce Suaeda tea, utilizing a synergistic blend of microbial agents: Kluyveromyces marxianus, Komagataeibacter europaeus, and Acetobacter schutzenbachii.

pmc-13095376.title: Comparison of Hospitalization Costs Associated With Human Metapneumovirus and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in US Adults
pmc-13095376.creator: Bradley K Ackerson, Emily Rayens, Lina S Sy, Hung Fu Tseng, Lei Qian, Yi Luo, Rachelle Juan, Xuan Huang, Jennifer H Ku, Punam P Modha, Radha M Bathala, Sudhir Venkatesan, Lisa Glasser, Richard McNulty, Daniel Molnar, Chengbin Wang, Jaejin An
pmc-13095376.description: Hospitalization costs on human metapneumovirus (hMPV) are needed to inform healthcare priorities, including vaccine and treatment development. Among 5775 adult hospitalizations with hMPV or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), hMPV was associated with shorter length of stay but greater frequency of pneumonia, resulting in adjusted mean costs comparable to RSV hospitalization.

pmc-13250733.title: Joint contribution of body mass index and psychological distress to short and long sickness absence among young and early midlife public sector employees: a register-linked follow-up study
pmc-13250733.creator: Mari-Liis Kalima, Tea Lallukka, Eira Roos, Jatta Valkonen, Anna C Svärd
pmc-13250733.description: Overweight/obesity and psychological distress often co-exist and are associated with sickness absence (SA). The objective of this study was to examine joint contribution of overweight/obesity and psychological distress on short and long SA periods, and to explore potential synergistic interactions between these factors.

pmc-13326393.title: Key role of transcription factors network in proliferative vitreoretinal diseases development
pmc-13326393.creator: Clément Duveau, Yosra Raiss El Harrak, Azine Datlibagi, Jason Perret, François Willermain, Christine Delporte, Elie Motulsky
pmc-13326393.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Proliferative vitreoretinal diseases (PVDs) encompass severe ocular disorders such as proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR), proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), and epiretinal membranes (ERM), characterized by the formation of fibrovascular membranes that often lead to retinal detachment and vision loss. A central mechanism driving these conditions is the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) of retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells, orchestrated by a network of transcription factors (TFs).

pmc-13406668.title: Exosomal EphA2 Promotes Gastric Cancer Progression by Inducing Phenotypic Transformation of Tumor Cells in a Ligand-Independent Manner
pmc-13406668.creator: Linan Zhan, Rui Wang, Furong Liu, Wanming Li, Jie Zhang, Xuetong Zhou, Wei Ba, Shuo Chen, Jin Fang
pmc-13406668.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The heterogeneity of tumor cells facilitates their dynamic adaptation to tumor microenvironmental pressures throughout progression. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying intercellular communication and transformation among heterogeneous tumor cells remain inadequately understood. In this study, we indicate that Ephrin type-A receptor 2 (EphA2) is heterogeneously expressed in gastric cancer (GC) tumor cells, with those exhibiting elevated EphA2 (EphA2High) expression demonstrating enhanced migratory and invasive capabilities.

pmc-13438377.creator: Peter Kwabena Appiah, Evelyn Yayra Bonney, Christian Obirikorang, James Odame Aboagye, Mildred Egyirba Hanson, Samuel Kwame Sopuruchi Agomuo, Alfred Effah, Max Efui Annani-Akollor, George Boateng Kyei
pmc-13438377.description: ObjectiveThis study investigated influence of cysteine-cysteine chemokines (CCR5, CCR5-59029A/G, CCR2), and stoma cell derived factor 1 (SDF1); as AIDS restriction genes (ARGs), on treatment outcomes among people with HIV (PWH) on long term antiretroviral therapy (ART) in Ghana.MethodsThis cross-sectional study was conducted among 167 PWH and receiving ART in Accra, Ghana.

pmc-13542546.title: Arthroscopic Bony Bankart Fixation Using Single-Row Technique with Knotless Suture Anchors
pmc-13542546.creator: George F Matta, Benjamin Brej, Samuel Taylor, Gregory L Cvetanovich, Jennifer Kurowicki, Ryan C Rauck
pmc-13542546.description: Background:Bony Bankart lesions involve detachment of the anteroinferior labrum with an associated glenoid rim fracture after traumatic anterior shoulder instability. Compared with isolated soft-tissue Bankart lesions, osseous involvement increases the risk of recurrent instability and progressive glenoid bone loss. Arthroscopic fixation techniques have evolved as minimally invasive alternatives to open repair and bone augmentation in appropriately selected cases.

pmc-13565383.title: Forearm Nonunion and Segmental Bone Defects: A Focused Review of Masquelet Reconstruction and Free Vascularized Bone Grafting
pmc-13565383.creator: Rita Saad, Johnny Saadeh, Fouad Assaf, Antoine Saber, Saadeddine Abouzahr, Elyssa Kiwan, Wendy Ghanem, Mohamad Badra, Ramzi Moucharafieh
pmc-13565383.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Segmental bone loss and chronic nonunion of the forearm present major reconstructive challenges due to the forearm’s unique functional anatomy and the frequent coexistence of biological compromise, infection, and soft-tissue deficiency. The purpose of this review is to analyze the pathophysiology of forearm nonunion and to compare the Masquelet induced membrane technique (IMT) and free vascularized bone grafting (VBG) as contemporary reconstructive strategies, focusing on indications, biological rationale, outcomes, and complications.
